fields.why: Table 2 reports per-variable p-values for group differences with no test named, and the article does not tie them to the GEE; the brief says such p-values imply an 'unnamed test'. A's reading (GEE term p-values) is plausible but not stated, and both readers' Table 2 groupwise omnibus entries rest on a test that A never records.
Follows from the unnamed Table 2 test (B's ancillary entry).

The Summary's comparative headline sets estimated infections against the reported count of confirmed cases (17,792), an external tally treated as fixed ('one of 10 infections', '9.6 times'). That makes the framework fixed referent. The Hispanic vs non-Hispanic pair appears only in the Results.

The nonrandom arm was defined by recruitment in two racial/ethnic minority communities, which is the article's own sampling definition, so race/ethnicity: population is defensible. Omitting it is also defensible, because that sample is 23% White and the main population is defined by state and age.
Race and ethnicity came from a participant-completed intake form, which supports self-identified. The brief makes basis optional, so B's omission is not wrong.

brief_issues: The brief does not say whether unattributed table p-values in a report that also fits a GEE are a separate 'unnamed test' or part of the model. It also does not say whether an external count (reported cases) compared with an estimate is a fixed referent or a pair.
